Brian Harvey CS61A context, Pig Latin rules

Hook: '¿puede un programa imprimir su propio código?', frames the 4-step journey
Code as string — half the program output, missing declaration
Template with hole — replace('X', s) — output has no quotes, fails
JSON.stringify(s) for escaping — WORKING QUINE (verified: 122 chars = 122 chars)
Same idea in Java with printf %c (34) %s — language-agnostic insight
'La recursión no es magia, es confianza' + where-recursion-lives + souvenir framing

what: Use captureRun (new Function + fake console) for real in-browser code execution
why: Browser natively runs JavaScript; alternative paths all fail in May 2026

alternatives_rejected.reason: Closed to public Feb 15 2026; new keys only for vetted educational use, not student projects
Requires precompiled .class/.jar bytecode; cannot compile source live in browser without bundling ECJ ≈ 10MB
All require API keys and have CORS or rate-limit issues from a static HTML file
External dependency could break mid-presentation; not self-contained

framing_used_with_audience: Honest: 'el navegador habla JavaScript, así que ejecuto JS — pero la lógica recursiva es idéntica a la de Java; mira el código Java al lado'. The JS variant is shown editable, the Java variant is shown read-only as classroom reference.

why: A working quine memorized is forgettable; a quine BUILT step-by-step with failed attempts is unforgettable

steps.lesson: Hello World — source ≠ output, the problem stated
Put code in a variable, print it — only half the program comes out
Template with placeholder X, replace X with s — close, but no quotes around s in output
Replace X with JSON.stringify(s) — adds the quotes and escaping — quine works

parallel_to_java: Java quine uses printf with %c+34 (ASCII for ") and %s to achieve the same escaping that JSON.stringify does in JS. The slide 12 places both side-by-side to drive the point home.

what: Sierpinski drawn by a REAL recursive JS function, not pre-rendered SVG
why: The visual literally IS recursion; depth=5 produces 243 triangles, staggered fade-in at 7ms intervals reveals the structure build itself; embodied learning

purpose: Working JavaScript quine — paso 4 of Tsoding journey
code:
const s = "const s = X;\nconsole.log(s.replace('X', JSON.stringify(s)));";
console.log(s.replace('X', JSON.stringify(s)));
verification_method: ran via Node.js with same captureRun logic used in the page; source.trim() === output.trim(); both 122 chars

purpose: Working Java quine (companion to the JS one, slide 12)
note: The String literal must be on ONE line in actual source; shown wrapped in slide with a comment.
verification_method: printf format string traced by hand: %c→", %s→s (with quotes from the surrounding %c%s%c), %c→", %n→newline; reproduces source exactly

edge_case_handled: Words with no vowels would infinite-loop. Not guarded in the playground because input is fixed test data; if students try 'rhythm' or 'crypt' they will hit stack overflow — explicitly note this as a discussion point if it happens.

name: captureRun
where: inline <script> at the bottom of recursion.html
summary: new Function('console', '"use strict";\n' + code)(fakeConsole) where fakeConsole captures .log/.error/.warn into an array. Returns {output, error}. The quine-check slides compare source.trim() === output.trim() and render a badge: '✓ es un quine' (green) or '✗ aún no' (red) with a diff position annotation.
safety: No DOM access from user code, no async, no eval. Errors caught and rendered in red in the terminal area.

keys.R: run the primary editor on the visible slide
keys.Tab inside textarea: insert two spaces, no focus jump

mouse: Click left half of slide → previous; click right half → next. Clicks inside editors, terminals, buttons, kbd, code are excluded.
reset_button: Each playground has a Reset button that restores the original code (snapshot taken at page load via ORIGINAL[] map)

tool: node — ran each ed-q1..ed-q4 textarea content through captureRun

results.paso_1: outputs 'Hola, mundo!' (12 chars) ≠ source (28 chars) — correctly NOT a quine
results.paso_2: outputs "console.log('Hola');" (20 chars) ≠ source (49 chars) — correctly NOT a quine
results.paso_3: outputs 87 chars ≠ source 90 chars; missing quotes around substituted s — correctly NOT a quine
results.paso_4: outputs 122 chars === source 122 chars, byte-identical — IS A QUINE ✓

observations: Strongly prefers iterative review before declaring done; pushes back when something feels off (asked to make it 'more realistic' rather than accepting initial keynote-style version)
Wants pedagogical authenticity: actual code execution beats simulated screenshots, even if it means switching language (Java→JS) to be honest about browser constraints
Drawn to 'thought process' content: Tsoding's iterative mistakes are seen as more valuable than the final clean answer
Aesthetic: dark, editorial, amber-accented; explicit aversion to generic-AI slide-deck look
Spanish-language deliverables for academic work; first-person 'yo / tú' tone with students, no usted
